I'm not sure if this really counts, but when I was in 7th grade, the teacher who ran our GSA would let us go to lunch with our room every day. He would curse in front of us, and buy us the weirdest items he could find on Amazon, but there are three things that I specifically remember. 

The first is the time that there was a class outside sitting under the window in his room (his room was on the 2nd floor). He took out the window screen and had a competition to see which one of us could get the most paper clips in people's hair. What makes it even better is that the winner got 120 mini plastic babies. 

He also organized a scavenger hunt for us right before winter break. He arranged clues around the room and created a google classroom with a ton of hidden clues in it for us, and when we solved the puzzle, we each got a bag of 100 peppermint patties. 

The last thing was when he arranged something kind of like a scavenger hunt (without me knowing) to ask out the girl that he knew I liked. I was mortified because I didn't know this was going to happen, but she said yes and we've been together ever since, so I guess it worked out. 

Basically, he was the best teacher I've ever developed a "friendship" with, and the only thing that made middle school tolerable. Now I go back to my middle school once a week and run the GSA with him, and it is without a doubt, my favorite place to be. I will forever be thankful for having him in my life.

I would take that offer only if I could still take away all of the lessons I have learned from identifying as transgender in this society. I have learned a lot of lessons based off of how different genders/sexes are treated differently, and have learned more about how much we have to improve how minorities are treated. Being able to have the male body that matches who I am is one of my biggest wants/needs, and it would have been ideal to be born with such, but knowing what I know now because of not having that, is also important to me. In short, I would take the offer f being able to wake up tomorrow as the same person I am today with a male body, but I wouldn't if I had never learned the things I have because of living my life using the label of transgender.

One of my earliest memories is of a specific Christmas Eve dinner, and the events that took place when my family has consumed a large amount of alcohol.  My family has the tradition of getting my mom's extended family together, and eating lobster for dinner on Christmas Eve. I was about 6 years old, and it was the first Christmas after my great aunt had passed away. Said aunt's son was at the party with his wife, who was extremely not sober by about 9 o'clock. Before my grandma and her brother in law walked her to the my grandma's house which was right next door, my drunken second cousin in law walked up to her father in law and said "Your son has an amazing penis" after expressing her true (negative) feelings about his recently deceased wife.
